## Summary

A long-running Meridian keeps growing in memory until it is restarted. On a busy OpenCode instance it reached 2-6 GB within a day and 9.4 GB after three and a half days, pushing the host into swap. Nearly all of that memory is identical copies of the same tool definitions.

Every OpenCode session sends the same tool list. Meridian builds that list into passthrough MCP definitions (Zod schemas) and keeps the result in the per-session `sessionMcpCache`, which holds up to `MERIDIAN_MAX_SESSIONS` (1,000) sessions. Each session built its own copy. For a 230-tool list one copy is about 650k schema objects, roughly 30 MB of heap, so a full cache held tens of copies of the same thing per GB.

After this change, sessions that send the same tools share one built set:

- `sharedPassthroughMcpServer` (in `src/proxy/passthroughTools.ts`) returns the same built set for the same content. The key is a digest of everything the build reads: tool names, descriptions, deferral flags, schemas in request order, the MCP namespace, the resolved auto-defer decision and the core tool names. A shared set is therefore exactly what a fresh build would produce. Each query still builds its own MCP server from the definitions, so the per-query transport behaviour is unchanged.
- The index holds sets through `WeakRef`s and drops a digest once its set is collected, so it keeps nothing alive. `sessionMcpCache` and the other session caches keep their existing bounds and still decide how long a set lives.
- `server.ts` calls it on a session cache miss instead of `createPassthroughMcpServer`.

Measured by driving the real server with a mocked SDK, 230 tools and a 100-session cache: heap 3,117 MB before, 108 MB after, both flat once the cache is full.

## Tests

- `src/__tests__/passthrough-shared-definitions.test.ts`: two sessions with identical tools are served from one built set (fails without the fix), and any input the build reads produces a separate set.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean; the passthrough suites (`passthrough-mcp-per-query`, `defer-pin`, `passthrough-tool-set-key`, `passthrough-tool-aliases`, `passthrough-tool-sort`, `passthrough-declared-schema`, `proxy-passthrough-oc-prefixed-tools`) pass.

This PR is AI generated, but under direct supervision and on request of @Nowaker.
